parsed_output.answer: To find the distance of the image formed by a concave mirror, we use the mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. Here, the object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of the mirror, so u = -10 cm (negative because the object is on the same side as the incoming light). The radius of curvature (R) is given as 8 cm, and the focal length (f) of a concave mirror is half the radius of curvature, so f = R/2 = 8/2 = 4 cm. Substituting the values into the mirror formula: 1/4 = 1/v + 1/(-10). Solving for 1/v gives 1/v = 1/4 + 1/10 = 5/20 + 2/20 = 7/20. Therefore, v = 20/7 ≈ 2.86 cm. The image is formed at a distance of approximately 2.86 cm in front of the mirror.
